capability.description: Uses Faker defaults to create a requested number of synthetic records, each containing name, email, and address fields; the declared schema argument is accepted but ignored.
capability.problem_space: Small synthetic contact datasets for tests or examples that need a fixed name/email/address record shape.

constraint.io_signature: Inputs: required schema string (ignored) and optional integer-like count string defaulting to 3; output: JSON records array of fake contacts.
accepted_inputs: any schema string, retained only for interface compatibility and not interpreted
an optional base-10 integer string for the number of records
constraint.output_shape: Success is an object with status="success", tool="lib.faker_generate", and records as an array whose entries each contain name, email, and address strings. A caught count-conversion or Faker generation exception produces an object with status="error", tool="lib.faker_generate", and message as the exception string, then exits with code 1.
limitations: ignores the schema argument and always emits exactly the name, email, and address fields
uses Faker's default locale and no caller-supplied seed, so output is not reproducible or locale-configurable
count defaults to 3; a negative count yields an empty array and a non-integer count returns an error
does not enforce uniqueness or validate relationships among generated fields

output_contract.description: Array of synthetic records with fixed name, email, and address fields.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: create sample names emails and addresses
negative_intents: generate records from a caller-defined schema
generate localized or unique datasets with validation rules
